The short answer

This page compares Maia with Instinct at instinct.com. Instinct's public site describes a personal assistant that connects to one person's apps and devices, accepts texts and calls, and uses signals such as email, messaging, screen, audio, and location. Maia has a narrower workplace focus. It gives a Slack channel a shared coworker with team-visible instructions, memory, tools, and approvals.

These products solve different ownership problems. Instinct may suit a person who wants ambient help with communication and logistics. Maia suits a company process that several people need to see, correct, and continue.

A project handoff

An operations team needs a daily project handoff. The source material is a Slack channel, a supplied tracker, and the team's definition of blocked work. The result should identify confirmed progress, unowned tasks, and the decisions the next shift must make.

With Maia, the request starts in the project channel. The channel coworker reads the permitted context, uses the team's handoff format, and posts a draft where people can correct it. A project lead reviews any proposed update to the connected tracker. The same coworker can prepare another handoff on a schedule and retain channel-specific corrections.

Instinct promises a personal assistant. A person can contact it by text or phone, and it can follow up on dropped threads and personal logistics. The site describes awareness across devices and communications. It does not publish enough detail to map the same shared handoff workflow, including channel identity, teammate access, or business audit controls.

Choose Maia when

Choose Maia when the work belongs to a team and Slack is the operating record. Team members can see why the coworker produced a result, add missing context, and pass ownership without moving the work into a private assistant account.

Maia also fits organizations that need explicit channel boundaries, named approvers, connected-app policy, scheduled team work, and model choice. Validate the exact app path and review behavior with a real task.

Choose Instinct when

Choose Instinct when personal awareness is the main requirement. Phone and text access, device context, proactive follow-up, and help with daily logistics go beyond Maia's stated workplace scope. Maia does not claim to read a person's screen, audio, or location, and it is not positioned as a personal life assistant.

Instinct.com does not publish a detailed security page, pricing, supported-country list, or business plan. Ask Instinct directly about credential storage, data retention, action approval, availability, and account administration.

Run a fair evaluation

Start with ownership and data boundaries. Write down who should see each request, which device or business sources are necessary, and who is accountable for an external action. Then test a routine that includes missing information and a step that needs human review.

For Maia, observe the Slack thread, connected-app identity, approval record, and channel memory. For Instinct, ask for a product demonstration that shows how the assistant distinguishes personal and company context, how it records actions, and whether another person can safely take over a task. Do not infer answers from the breadth of a landing-page promise.

Common questions

What is Instinct AI?

This comparison covers the personal assistant at instinct.com, which describes using applications and device context and communicating through calls and texts.

Is Instinct for businesses?

The reviewed official site does not document team roles, business plans, shared channels, or enterprise administration. Ask the vendor for current details if company deployment is the goal.

Does Maia use screen, audio, or location data?

Maia's public product focuses on Slack context and authorized connected apps. It does not market ambient access to a person's screen, audio, or location.
